title: Block acceleration correct
description: Essential: Student states the block's acceleration as 2 m/s² to the right, derived from kinetic friction μmg = ma₁.

title: Cart acceleration correct
description: Essential: Student states the cart's acceleration as 0.5 m/s² to the right, derived from F - μmg = Ma₂.

title: Time to common speed
description: Essential: Student calculates the time for the block and cart to reach a common speed as 1 s, using kinematics v₀ + a₂t = a₁t.

title: Block speed at t=1.5 s
description: Essential: Student finds the block's speed at t=1.5 s as 2.4 m/s, correctly handling the two acceleration phases.

title: Identifies two motion phases
description: Important: Student recognizes that after reaching common speed, the block and cart move together with a single acceleration.

title: Checks for slipping after t₁
description: Important: Student verifies that the required frictional force for joint motion (ma₃) is less than the maximum static friction.

title: Correct kinematics application
description: Important: Student correctly applies constant-acceleration equations (v = v₀ + at) for both objects in each phase.

title: Sign/direction error
description: Pitfall: Student misassigns the direction of friction on the cart or block, leading to incorrect acceleration signs.

title: Forgets initial cart velocity
description: Pitfall: Student sets up the common-speed equation without including the cart's initial velocity v₀.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student explicitly shows units in calculations and confirms they are consistent (e.g., using g=10 m/s²).
